title: GYM-QR
subtitle: Attendance and locker management for a single gym
thesis: One session per member. One key per locker.
role: System analysis, requirements, system design, implementation
status: Backend milestones M0–M5 complete; member, cashier and admin interfaces still provisional
boundary: This is a self-initiated system concept built from my own observation of how gyms run their front desk. No gym owner commissioned it, no gym owner approved the requirements, and it has not been deployed or used by real members. Everything below is either implemented behaviour, a documented requirement, or a stated assumption, never a measured business result.

observe.context: A mid-sized gym records daily attendance in a paper book at the front desk. Membership status is checked by eye, and locker keys are handed out with no record of who holds which key. The same person works the desk during the busiest hour, so the queue is a side effect of the recording method, not of the number of members.

hypotheses.text: The front desk is the bottleneck at peak hours because every member stops there, including members who do not need a locker.
Locker keys go missing because nothing links a key to a session.
Expired memberships are hard to enforce at the desk under time pressure.

observe.note: These are hypotheses drawn from observation, not findings from interviews. Validating them would require time at a real gym with the owner and the staff, that is the first thing I would do next.

actors.need: Check in quickly, see package status and locker number
Be activated by the cashier without an account first
See arrivals as they happen, verify identity, allocate keys
Visit and peak-hour reports, manage packages and lockers

frictions.asIs: Queue at the desk, name written by hand
frictions.toBe: Member states locker need in the app, scans a static QR, walks in
frictions.leak: Every member waits, including those who need nothing from the desk

frictions.asIs: Cashier reads a card or remembers the face
frictions.toBe: Server evaluates effective_status on every scan
frictions.leak: Expired members can pass at peak time

frictions.toBe: Atomic assignment to one open session, with audit entry
frictions.leak: Two people can hold the same key; no trace of who holds it

frictions.asIs: Book is closed, keys are counted by hand
frictions.toBe: Batch reset closes sessions and frees lockers

analyse.insight: The queue is not solved by making the scan faster. It is solved by moving the locker question out of the queue: a member who needs no locker should never stop at the desk. That single decision (D3) removed the mandatory stop for most arrivals, and it also created the constraint that made the session model necessary.

in: Member web app (PWA) with OTP login, QR scan, GPS validation, digital card, locker status
Cashier dashboard with real-time feed, locker assignment, manual check-in, package sales
Admin panel for packages, locker assets, reports and gym settings

modules.name: Member app
modules.sample: FR-MEM-03 geofence validation with accuracy tolerance; FR-MEM-04 one open session per member

modules.name: Cashier dashboard
modules.sample: FR-CAS-02 atomic locker assignment; FR-CAS-05 manual check-in with audit reason

modules.name: Admin and data

modules.name: Non-functional
modules.sample: Response p95 ≤ 1.5 s; UTC storage with Asia/Jakarta display; data retention

decisions.decision: Expired members are rejected by the server, and the cashier gets a renewal alert
decisions.reason: Keeps the rule out of the hands of a cashier working a queue
decisions.rejected: Allow entry with a red warning in the feed

decisions.decision: The member states locker need in the app before scanning
decisions.reason: Removes the mandatory desk stop for members without a locker

decisions.decision: One open session per member, plus a 5-minute rescan guard
decisions.reason: A longer cooldown did not prevent duplicates and blocked legitimate re-entry

decisions.decision: Locker assignment is atomic: transaction with a row lock
decisions.reason: Two cashiers can pick the same number at the same moment

decisions.decision: Geofence radius is configurable, with GPS accuracy tolerance and a manual fallback
decisions.reason: Indoor GPS accuracy cannot be guaranteed to 30 m

verify.summary: Every expected behaviour was written as a numbered acceptance scenario before it was implemented. Fifteen scenarios exist (AT-01 to AT-15). The repository records no manual UAT run: the evidence column in docs/UAT.md is empty. What can be checked today is the automated suite.

uat.step: Active member scans the QR at the desk
uat.expected: 200, one attendance row, card appears on the dashboard in under 500 ms

uat.step: Scan using a photo of the QR from inside the gym
Scan while a session is still open
Two requests with the same Idempotency-Key
Two cashiers assign locker #05 at the same time

uat.expected: Locker available, checkout_time filled, member sees the change
403, no attendance row, appears in rejected scans with an audit entry
Coordinates NULL, manual_reason filled, audit entry present

uat.step: Day pass used on two consecutive days
Cashier offline for 10 minutes while members keep scanning
uat.expected: Check-ins stored, sessions appear after reconnect

uat.step: Batch reset with the wrong count

errors.condition: Distance greater than radius plus reported accuracy
Member already has an open session
Another cashier holds the locker row
Scan within rescan_guard_seconds of a closed session

reflect.demonstrates: That I can take a process I only observed, decide what the system should and should not do, write it down so another person could build it, and define how to check the result.
limits: The process analysis is not validated with a gym owner or staff; the frictions above are hypotheses.
No business result exists: no deployment, no measured queue time, no member feedback.
The interfaces are provisional, so the workflow has not been tested with a real cashier under pressure.
The geofence radius is uncalibrated at a real location, and GPS accuracy indoors is a known weak point (PRD §8.1).
next: Spend time at a gym with the owner and staff, and replace the hypotheses with observations.
Fix the one static-analysis error and keep CI green so the suite result is visible to anyone.
Run the 15 acceptance scenarios by hand and fill the evidence column with real output.
Calibrate the geofence radius on site, and test the scan flow with a cashier during peak hours.
